description:
FILED s473t4 (#1501 CHECK 2 round 1, 2026-09-13).  t/op/cproto.t's 183 diverging rows are ONE cluster: the file loops over perl's keyword list and asserts `prototype("CORE::$keyword")`.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    for my $kw (qw(abs length ref push sprintf lc)) {
        my $p = prototype("CORE::$kw");
        print "$kw=", (defined $p ? "($p)" : "undef"), "\n";
    }
    eval { prototype("CORE::nosuchthing") };
    print "err=", ($@ ? "yes" : "no"), "\n";

    perl:  abs=(_) length=(_) ref=(_) push=(\@@) sprintf=($@) lc=(_)  err=yes
    pcl :  abs=undef  length=undef  ref=undef  push=undef  sprintf=undef  lc=undef  err=no

So THREE answers are wrong at once: a defined prototype reads undef; the "unknown keyword" case does not throw ("Can't find an opnumber for ..."); and the keywords whose real answer IS undef (the 50-odd control-flow words) pass only by accident.

WHAT IT WOULD TAKE: perl's prototype strings for the ~180 prototyped builtins.  That is LANGUAGE DATA, not module data, so it belongs in the runtime (CLAUDE.md 9a's core-builtin exception) -- but it is not PCL's existing `Pl/PExpr/Config.pm known_no_of_params` table, which records ARITIES for parsing, not perl's prototype TEXT (`\@@`, `$@`, `_`, `;$`, `*`).  The two tables would then have to agree, so the honest shape is ONE table with both facts, generated once from perl's own answers and checked by a guard row.

RELATED and probably the same round: #1577 (`&CORE::NAME` is not an addressable sub, op/coreamp.t 723 rows).  Both say "PCL has no model of the CORE:: package".  Round t5b.

VALUE: 183 rows in one file, plus whatever op/attrproto.t (31) and op/protowarn.t (8) share.

=== DONE (s484a) ===

SHIPPED s484a (Opus, 2026-09-13).  THE TABLE IS GENERATED, NOT TYPED.

`%pcl-core-prototypes` now lives in `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` -- perl's prototype
strings are LANGUAGE data, the same kind of fact as an operator's precedence
(CLAUDE.md 9a's core-builtin exception) -- but they are ~180 strings perl alone
is the authority for, and a hand-typed copy is a copy that drifts silently.  So
`tools/gen-core-protos.pl` asks the LIVE perl for every one, and
`--check` re-asks and diffs as a row of `Pl/t/core-proto-01.t`.
253 keywords, 182 with a prototype.

THE VALUES vs THE LIST are two different problems and the tool says so:
  * THE VALUES are always a live `eval { prototype "CORE::$kw" }`.
  * THE LIST cannot be enumerated from a running perl -- `%CORE::` is EMPTY
    (keyword subs are autovivified on demand; measured) and there is no
    `keys %keywords` -- so the candidates are the UNION of perl's own
    `t/op/cproto.t` `__DATA__` NAMES (found through PCLPaths::perl_suite_t,
    never a written-down path) and every name in `Pl::PExpr::Config`'s
    `known_no_of_params`.  ONLY THE NAMES are read from that file; its
    expectations are the ORACLE and are never copied, which is what keeps the
    guard row non-circular.

ALL THREE OF PERL'S ANSWERS, and `%p-core-prototype` is the one place they are
written down:
  * a keyword with a prototype -> its string (`abs` `_`, `push` `\@@`,
    `sprintf` `$@`, `open` `*;$@`, `chdir` `;$`, `__FILE__` the DEFINED empty
    string)
  * a keyword without one      -> undef (`if`, `my`, `print`, `split`, ~70
    control-flow words -- these used to "pass" by accident)
  * anything else              -> `Can't find an opnumber for "NAME"`, which
    quotes the name WITHOUT the CORE:: prefix (`CORE::Foo::bar` names
    `Foo::bar`, `CORE::GLOBAL::x` names `GLOBAL::x`)
  * and THE ONE EXCEPTION a blanket rule-12 die would have got wrong:
    `prototype("CORE::")` -- the EMPTY name -- is undef, NOT a fatal (probed).

23-row probe vs perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s484a/probes/p1586.pl): 21 IDENTICAL.
The two that differ are rows 18/19, the BLESSED classic-prototype gap
(`sub f ($$)` is consumed at transpile time) -- docs/not-supported.md
"`prototype()` -- returns only registered prototypes", whose section now says
the CORE:: half works and that a user sub is never looked up in the CORE table.

THE DISAGREEMENT IS MEASURED, NOT UNIFIED (this task's own bar).
`known_no_of_params` records ARITIES for parsing, not prototype TEXT.
`tools/gen-core-protos.pl --arity` compares each generated prototype's implied
arity against the Config spec and is a guard row:

    keywords with both facts: 151
      perl answers undef (the prototype says nothing): 17
      Config spec is a LIST spec (admits every arity):  46
      actually COMPARED:                                88
      DISAGREEING:                                       0

So there is NOTHING TO FILE -- the two tables do not contradict wherever they
can be compared, and the "one table with both facts" #1586 floated has no bug
behind it.  ITS FIRST READING SAID 12, and all twelve were the TOOL reading a
`\[%@]` reference-group as a slurpy `@`: a `\[$@%*]` group is ONE argument, and
`proto_arity` now consumes it as one token before looking for a bare slurpy.

GUARD `Pl/t/core-proto-01.t` (11 rows; 6 of the 9 non-skipped ones FAIL on a
`2ffefb36` archive extraction, and the 2 table rows SKIP there because the tool
does not exist yet).  Four rows are inverse guards: the control-flow undefs,
the empty-name non-fatal, a user sub never looked up in the CORE table, and a
sub NAMED like a keyword (`sub length` stays undef while `CORE::length` is `_`).

ONE LESSON FOR ANY FUTURE GENERATED LISP: the block must be generated in the
repo formatter's OWN indentation (the `.lisp` PostToolUse hook re-indents a
LOOP clause's argument to align under the clause word), or `--check` reports a
phantom DRIFT the first time the file is touched.  It did, once.

#1577 IS NOT IN SCOPE, and what the table makes cheap for it: `&CORE::NAME` as
an addressable sub needs (a) a CODE object per keyword and (b) the knowledge of
which names ARE keywords and what arity each takes.  (b) is now one hash
lookup away -- `%pcl-core-prototypes` holds every keyword and its prototype, so
`defined &{"CORE::$kw"}` and the arity check `&CORE::push` needs are table
reads rather than a new enumeration.  (a) is still the work: a wrapper per
keyword that forwards to the runtime primitive, which is where op/coreamp.t's
723 rows live.

BARS: full sweep (a `cl/` change is invisible to corpus-diff) + the op/
companion leg on cproto/attrproto/protowarn; `tools/ir-host-leak.pl`
byte-identical to base.  Numbers in DECIDED.md sec s484a and the session log.
subject: `prototype("CORE::NAME")` returns undef for EVERY builtin -- op/cproto.t 183 rows, one cluster, one cause
